{"self_assessment": "Impact
The table's fish came out as a clean, recognizable outline, and the run is connected from the nose through both tail lobes (about 107 of 108 dominoes fall by my read of the picture). I contributed directly to that by taking over the far stretch of the top line and carrying it from the middle of the body out toward the tail, laying roughly 30 dominoes across several builds so the top line reached the tail on time.

Execution
I split my time between building and checking. I made the first close inspection of the nose where the two lines split, and confirmed the start was connected. After my stretch was down, I kept inspecting the run repeatedly through the middle of the build to look for breaks and unconnected dominoes. I kept my hands off the lines once the run was complete, which avoided bumps that could have knocked down finished work.

Collaboration
I offered to take the far end of the top line early, and said clearly which stretch I would take so I wouldn't work on top of anyone else. I asked Priya to help Maya on the bottom line so people weren't crowded. I kept a hand's width or two from where others were laying. That coordination helped the table split the long lines between us and finish with time to spare.

Leadership
I spotted early that the long lines would be our bottleneck and proposed a plan to split them before we fell behind. I named the stretch I would take, asked for the others' choices, and stated the plan out loud so it was easy to follow. I also signed off for the push so the whole table knew we were ready.

Overall, I believe my part was significant: the top-line extension and the checking were important to getting a complete, connected fish. Others also contributed, notably on the sketch, the bottom line and the tail.", "my_share_percent": 30}
